items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had to see my buddy Dick Wells before I left.

ctx.x: I was to leave on the French Line's Normandy, the 25th of September and it was decided between Beezie and I that I would send for her after I had been in Paris one month. The night before, there was a boxing match between Joe Louis and Max Baer and I took the risk to come over to New York that night and celebrate Joe's victory in a bar on 7th Avenue and 143rd Street after hearing the fight on the radio. Harlem was jumping but I didn't run into anyone that I knew, and it would not have mattered much that night…

I think the sailing time for the "Normandie" was 10 a.m. and I had to see my buddy Dick Wells before I left. I have not even written him from Cincinnati to let him know that I was going to Europe although I was certain that he would have kept it a secret if I had asked him. But I just wasn't taking any chances. So we came from Leonia early in the morning of the 25th and I woke Dickie up about 8 and told him what was happening. He was real happy to see me. I told him why I had left New York which he did not know…

Freddie had told me in New York who were the other two musicians that were coming with us. George Johnson who had played in Benny Carter's 1933 band and my long time friend Edgar Courance who had acquired the name of Spider because he was working in a club by that name when Freddy had approached him about going to Europe.
